statute_title: Driving or Having Control of Vehicle While Under Influence (DWUI)
elements: Defendant drove or had actual physical control of a vehicle
Within Wyoming on a public street or highway
While under the influence of alcohol, a controlled substance, or a combination
Or had a BAC of .08 or higher
enhancements: BAC .15 or higher (aggravated DWUI — enhanced penalties)
Passenger under 16 (additional penalties — up to 1 year for first; up to 5 years for second+ with child passenger)
Fourth conviction within 10 years (felony — up to 7 years)
notes: Wyoming uses 'DWUI' (Driving While Under the Influence). Implied consent under § 31-6-102. Admin license suspension 90 days first offense. Ignition interlock may be ordered.

elements: Defendant drove or had actual physical control of a vehicle
While under the influence of alcohol or drugs
BAC .08 or higher, or impairment of driving ability
No prior DWUI convictions within 10 years
enhancements: BAC .15 or higher (aggravated — mandatory jail and increased suspension)
Passenger under 16 (up to 1 year jail and $1,000 fine)
notes: First offense may qualify for deferred prosecution or treatment court. 90-day license suspension. Ignition interlock may be ordered for BAC .15+.

elements: Defendant drove or had actual physical control of a vehicle
While under the influence of alcohol or drugs
BAC .08 or higher, or impairment of driving ability
One or more prior DWUI convictions within 10 years
enhancements: Passenger under 16 (enhanced — up to 5 years for second+ with child)
notes: 10-year lookback period for counting prior offenses. Fourth offense within 10 years is a felony. License revocation 1 year (second); 3 years (third+).

offense_class: Same as alcohol DWUI by offense count
penalty_max: Same as alcohol DWUI by offense count
fine_max: Same as alcohol DWUI by offense count
elements: Defendant drove or had actual physical control of a vehicle
While under the influence of a controlled substance
Or under the combined influence of alcohol and a controlled substance
To a degree which renders the defendant incapable of safely driving
mandatory_minimum: Same as alcohol DWUI by offense count
enhancements: Combined influence of alcohol and drugs
Presence of Schedule I or II substance
notes: No per se drug limit in Wyoming. Prosecution must prove actual impairment. Drug Recognition Expert (DRE) testimony commonly used. Includes prescription medications.

elements: Defendant drove a vehicle on a highway
In willful or wanton disregard for the safety of persons or property
notes: Common plea-down from DWUI. License suspension possible. Points added to driving record.

statute_title: Duty to Stop at Accident — Injury or Death
elements: Defendant was the driver of a vehicle involved in an accident
Accident resulted in injury, death, or property damage
Defendant knowingly failed to stop at the scene
Defendant failed to provide identification and render aid
notes: Hit-and-run involving death carries up to 10 years. Property damage only is a misdemeanor under § 31-5-1103. License revocation upon conviction.

statute_title: Homicide by Vehicle — While Under the Influence
elements: Defendant operated a vehicle while under the influence of alcohol or drugs
Defendant's impaired operation caused the death of another person
notes: Vehicular homicide while under the influence carries up to 20 years. Non-DUI vehicular homicide (criminally negligent) under § 6-2-106(a) carries up to 10 years.

elements: Defendant operated a vehicle in a criminally negligent manner
Defendant's operation caused the death of another person
Without intoxication as a factor
notes: Non-DUI vehicular homicide based on criminal negligence. Less serious than DUI-related vehicular homicide.

statute_title: Driving While License Canceled, Suspended, or Revoked
elements: Defendant drove a motor vehicle on a public highway
Defendant's license was suspended, revoked, or canceled
Defendant had knowledge of the suspension or revocation
enhancements: Habitual traffic offender (felony — up to 5 years)
notes: Habitual traffic offender designation requires 3+ convictions for serious offenses within 5 years. Driving on habitual offender status is a felony.

statute_title: Fleeing or Attempting to Elude a Police Officer
elements: A law enforcement officer gave a visual or audible signal to stop
Defendant was operating a motor vehicle
Defendant willfully failed to stop
Defendant attempted to flee or elude the officer
notes: Basic fleeing is a misdemeanor. Aggravated fleeing (reckless driving or injury) is a felony. License revocation upon conviction.

offense_class: Misdemeanor (first/second); Felony (third+ or Schedule I/II amounts exceeding threshold)
penalty_max: 1 year (misdemeanor); 5 years (felony — third+ or large amounts)
elements: Defendant knowingly or intentionally possessed a controlled substance
Without a valid prescription or legal authority
Substance is listed in Schedules I through V
enhancements: Third or subsequent offense (felony — up to 5 years)
notes: First and second possession offenses are misdemeanors. Third offense is a felony. Drug court and diversion programs available for first offenders.

statute_title: Possession of Marijuana (3 oz or Less)
elements: Defendant knowingly or intentionally possessed marijuana
Amount of 3 ounces or less
Without legal authority
enhancements: More than 3 oz (felony — possession with intent)
notes: Wyoming has not legalized recreational or medical marijuana. Possession of 3 oz or less is a misdemeanor. Over 3 oz may trigger possession with intent charges.

elements: Defendant knowingly or intentionally possessed cocaine
Cocaine is a Schedule II controlled substance
Without a valid prescription
notes: Simple possession of cocaine is a misdemeanor for first/second offenses. Third offense is a felony.

elements: Defendant knowingly or intentionally possessed methamphetamine
Methamphetamine is a Schedule II controlled substance
Without a valid prescription
notes: Simple meth possession is a misdemeanor for first/second offenses. Manufacturing methamphetamine is a separate felony under § 35-7-1031(a).

statute_title: Manufacture or Delivery of Controlled Substance — Schedule I or II Narcotic
elements: Defendant manufactured, delivered, or possessed with intent to deliver
A narcotic drug classified in Schedule I or II
Including heroin, cocaine, fentanyl, or methamphetamine
notes: Schedule I/II narcotic delivery carries the highest penalties. Second offense doubles the maximum. School zone enhancement under § 35-7-1036.

penalty_max: 10 years (Schedule I-II non-narcotic); 5 years (Schedule III); 2 years (Schedule IV); 1 year (Schedule V)
elements: Defendant manufactured, delivered, or possessed with intent to deliver
A non-narcotic controlled substance
From Schedule I through V
notes: Non-narcotic Schedule I-II (hallucinogens, amphetamines) carry up to 10 years. Schedule V delivery is a misdemeanor.

elements: Defendant manufactured or attempted to manufacture a controlled substance
Through chemical synthesis, cultivation, or processing
notes: Clandestine lab operations carry additional cleanup and restitution costs. Child endangerment charges added if minors present.

elements: Defendant possessed drug paraphernalia
Knowing or intending it to be used for manufacturing, testing, or consuming a controlled substance
enhancements: Delivery of paraphernalia to a minor (felony — up to 5 years)
notes: Delivery of paraphernalia to a minor under 18 is a felony. Personal use paraphernalia is a misdemeanor.

statute_title: Possession with Intent to Manufacture or Deliver
penalty_max: 20 years (Schedule I-II narcotic); 10 years (Schedule I-II non-narcotic); 5 years (Schedule III)
elements: Defendant possessed a controlled substance
With intent to manufacture or deliver
Intent inferred from quantity, packaging, scales, cash, or communications
notes: Marijuana over 3 oz may trigger PWID charges. Intent is inferred from circumstantial evidence including quantity and packaging.

penalty_max: Death or life imprisonment without parole
elements: Defendant purposely and with premeditated malice killed another person
Or killed another while in perpetration of certain felonies (felony murder)
notes: Wyoming retains the death penalty. Life without parole is an alternative. Felony murder applies to deaths during arson, sexual assault, robbery, burglary, kidnapping, or escape.

elements: Defendant purposely and maliciously killed another person
Without premeditation
notes: Second degree murder requires malice but not premeditation. Includes depraved heart murder — extreme recklessness showing indifference to human life.

elements: Defendant unlawfully killed another person
Without malice
Voluntarily, upon a sudden heat of passion
notes: Heat of passion must arise from adequate provocation. Cooling-off period negates the defense.

elements: Defendant unlawfully killed another person
Without malice
While in the commission of an unlawful act not amounting to a felony
Or through criminal negligence
notes: Involuntary manslaughter in Wyoming carries the same statutory maximum as voluntary manslaughter. Sentencing depends on circumstances.

elements: Defendant caused or attempted to cause serious bodily injury to another person
Or threatened another with a deadly weapon
Intentionally, knowingly, or recklessly under circumstances manifesting extreme indifference to human life
enhancements: Against a law enforcement officer, firefighter, or emergency personnel (§ 6-5-204)
notes: Aggravated assault is a felony carrying up to 10 years. Assault on a peace officer is enhanced under § 6-5-204.

elements: Defendant intentionally, knowingly, or recklessly caused bodily injury to another person
Or made physical contact of an insulting or provoking nature
notes: Simple battery in Wyoming is a misdemeanor. Simple assault (threatening without contact) under § 6-2-501(a) is also a misdemeanor.

elements: Defendant intentionally, knowingly, or recklessly caused bodily injury to another person
enhancements: Causing serious bodily injury (aggravated assault — felony)
Use of deadly weapon (aggravated assault — felony)
notes: Battery is the base-level physical contact offense. Elevation to aggravated assault occurs with serious bodily injury or deadly weapon.

elements: Defendant took property from the person or presence of another
By use of force, threats, or intimidation
Against the will of the victim
enhancements: Use of a deadly weapon (aggravated robbery)
notes: Basic robbery in Wyoming carries 2-10 years. Aggravated robbery with deadly weapon is separately charged.

statute_title: Aggravated Robbery — Armed with a Deadly Weapon
elements: Defendant committed robbery
While armed with a deadly weapon or displaying what appeared to be a deadly weapon
Or intentionally inflicted or attempted to inflict bodily injury
notes: Aggravated robbery carries 5-25 years with a mandatory minimum. One of the most seriously punished property crimes in Wyoming.

penalty_max: Life imprisonment (if victim physically injured or not released safely)
elements: Defendant unlawfully removed another person from the place where found
Or unlawfully confined another person
With intent to hold for ransom, use as a hostage, facilitate a felony, inflict injury, or terrorize
mandatory_minimum: 20 years (if released unharmed); life (if injured or not released)
notes: Kidnapping carries severe mandatory minimums — 20 years minimum if victim is released unharmed, life if injured.

elements: Defendant intentionally started a fire or caused an explosion
Damaging a dwelling or occupied structure
Or when another person was present
notes: Second degree arson (§ 6-3-102) covers non-occupied structures — up to 10 years. Third degree (§ 6-3-103) covers personal property — up to 5 years.

penalty_max: 20 years (or one grade below completed offense)
elements: Defendant had specific intent to kill another person
Defendant performed an overt act toward committing murder
The murder was not completed
notes: Wyoming punishes attempts at maximum one class below the completed offense. Attempted first degree murder is a serious felony.

elements: Defendant threatened another person with a deadly weapon
Or used a deadly weapon to cause bodily injury
enhancements: Victim is a law enforcement officer
notes: Assault with a deadly weapon is charged as aggravated assault in Wyoming.

elements: Defendant took and carried away the personal property of another
With intent to permanently deprive the owner
enhancements: Livestock theft (felony regardless of value under § 6-3-403)
notes: Felony larceny threshold is $1,000. Livestock theft is always a felony in Wyoming.

elements: Defendant took and carried away the personal property of another
With intent to permanently deprive the owner
Value of property $1,000 or more
notes: Wyoming's felony theft threshold is $1,000.

elements: Defendant took and carried away the personal property of another
With intent to permanently deprive the owner
Value of property less than $1,000
notes: Petit larceny is a misdemeanor in Wyoming.

elements: Defendant concealed unpurchased merchandise of a retail establishment
Or altered a price tag
With intent to deprive the merchant of the merchandise
notes: Wyoming has a specific shoplifting statute. Civil recovery available to retailers.

elements: Defendant entered or remained in a building, occupied structure, or vehicle
Without authority
With intent to commit larceny or a felony therein
enhancements: Aggravated burglary — armed or causing injury (§ 6-3-301(c) — up to 25 years)
notes: Basic burglary is up to 10 years. Aggravated burglary (armed, causing bodily injury, or using a deadly weapon) carries up to 25 years.

elements: Defendant entered or remained in a dwelling
Without authority
With intent to commit larceny or a felony therein
enhancements: Aggravated — armed with deadly weapon or causing injury (up to 25 years)
notes: Wyoming does not separately classify residential burglary — same statute covers all structures. Sentencing typically higher for dwellings.

statute_title: Grand Larceny — Motor Vehicle / Unauthorized Use
elements: Defendant took a motor vehicle belonging to another
Without consent of the owner
With intent to permanently deprive or temporarily use
notes: Permanent theft of a vehicle is grand larceny. Unauthorized temporary use (joyriding) under § 31-11-103 is a separate felony.

elements: Defendant received, retained, or disposed of property of another
Knowing or having reasonable cause to believe the property was stolen
notes: Penalty mirrors the value thresholds of the underlying theft — $1,000 divides felony from misdemeanor.

elements: Defendant knowingly and intentionally destroyed or damaged property of another
Without the owner's consent
notes: Felony threshold is $1,000 in damages. Restitution typically ordered.

elements: Defendant entered or remained on property of another
Without permission or lawful authority
After being notified to leave or seeing no-trespassing signs
enhancements: Trespass to collect data (agricultural/ranch operations — enhanced under § 6-3-414)
notes: Wyoming has specific ag-gag trespass laws for data collection on agricultural operations. Posted land with signs or paint creates constructive notice.

elements: Defendant intentionally or recklessly damaged property of another
Without the owner's consent
notes: Wyoming uses 'destruction of property' rather than 'criminal mischief.' Value of damage determines penalty tier.

elements: Defendant caused bodily injury to a household member
Household member includes spouse, former spouse, person with child in common, cohabitant, or dating partner
By intentional, knowing, or reckless conduct
notes: First and second domestic battery are misdemeanors. Third within Wyoming is a felony. No mandatory arrest but officers encouraged to arrest. Protective orders under § 35-21-104.

elements: Defendant caused bodily injury to a household member
By intentional, knowing, or reckless conduct
One or more prior domestic battery convictions
notes: Third domestic battery in Wyoming is a felony. Federal firearms prohibition applies to DV misdemeanor convictions under 18 U.S.C. § 922(g)(9).

elements: Defendant recklessly engaged in conduct
That placed a child in danger of death or serious bodily injury
enhancements: Resulting in bodily injury (aggravated assault charges possible)
notes: Child endangerment is often charged alongside DUI when a child is present. Also applies to leaving children in dangerous environments.

elements: Defendant intentionally or recklessly caused physical injury to a child under 16
Or subjected a child to cruel or unreasonable punishment
notes: Child abuse resulting in serious bodily injury carries up to 25 years. Death of a child through abuse is charged as homicide.

statute_title: Violation of an Order of Protection
elements: A valid order of protection was in effect
Defendant had knowledge of the order
Defendant knowingly violated the terms of the order
enhancements: Second or subsequent violation within 5 years (felony)
notes: First violation is a misdemeanor. Repeat violations within 5 years elevate to felony.

offense_class: Misdemeanor (first); Felony (second+ or violation of protective order)
elements: Defendant engaged in a course of conduct directed at a specific person
That would cause a reasonable person to fear for safety or suffer emotional distress
Defendant intended to harass, frighten, or intimidate
enhancements: Second or subsequent offense (felony — up to 10 years)
In violation of a protective order (felony)
Aggravated stalking — credible threat of violence (felony)
notes: Aggravated stalking involving credible threats of death or serious bodily harm is a felony. Course of conduct requires 2+ acts.

elements: Defendant engaged in a pattern of conduct with intent to harass another person
Conduct served no legitimate purpose
And would cause a reasonable person to feel harassed
notes: Harassment is a lesser offense than stalking. Includes telephone harassment and electronic communications.

statute_title: Abuse, Neglect, or Exploitation of a Vulnerable Adult
elements: Defendant was a caretaker for a vulnerable adult
Defendant intentionally or recklessly abused, neglected, or exploited the vulnerable adult
notes: Financial exploitation of a vulnerable adult is a separate offense. Adult Protective Services involvement required.

statute_title: Possession of a Firearm by a Prohibited Person
elements: Defendant possessed a firearm
Defendant was prohibited from possessing firearms (convicted violent felon, involuntarily committed, fugitive)
notes: Wyoming is a constitutional carry state — no permit needed for concealed carry by lawful citizens. Prohibitions apply to violent felons and certain other persons.

statute_title: Possession of Firearm by Convicted Violent Felon
elements: Defendant possessed a firearm
Defendant had previously been convicted of a violent felony
Or attempted violent felony
notes: Wyoming only prohibits firearm possession for violent felons, not all felons. Non-violent felons may possess firearms. Federal law (18 U.S.C. § 922(g)) still applies to all felons.

statute_title: Carrying a Concealed Weapon — Prohibited Persons
elements: Defendant carried a concealed deadly weapon
Defendant was a prohibited person or under disqualification
notes: Wyoming enacted constitutional carry — no permit needed for lawful gun owners. Only prohibited persons (violent felons, etc.) face concealed carry charges.

elements: Defendant discharged a firearm
In a reckless manner endangering the safety of another person
notes: Reckless discharge is a misdemeanor unless injury occurs, at which point aggravated assault charges may apply.

statute_title: Unauthorized Use of Personal Identifying Information
elements: Defendant used personal identifying information of another person
Without the authorization or consent of that person
With intent to obtain anything of value or cause harm
notes: Includes Social Security numbers, financial account information, and biometric data. Restitution to victims required.

elements: Defendant was entrusted with property of another
Defendant fraudulently converted the property to own use
With intent to deprive the owner
notes: Embezzlement by public officers carries enhanced penalties. General embezzlement follows larceny value thresholds.

elements: Defendant falsely made, completed, or altered a written instrument
With intent to defraud or deceive another
Instrument includes checks, deeds, contracts, wills, public records
notes: Uttering (passing) a forged instrument (§ 6-3-603) carries the same penalties.

elements: Defendant obtained property of another by false pretenses
Through misrepresentation or deception
With intent to defraud
notes: General fraud statute covers false pretenses, confidence games, and scheme-based fraud.

statute_title: Fraudulent Use of a Credit Card
elements: Defendant used a credit or debit card
Knowing it was stolen, forged, revoked, or expired
With intent to obtain money, goods, or services
notes: Includes possession of a stolen or forged card and unauthorized use. Multiple transactions may be aggregated.

fine_max: $10,000 or twice the value of the property
elements: Defendant conducted a financial transaction
Involving proceeds known to be derived from criminal activity
With intent to promote or conceal the criminal activity
notes: Includes structuring transactions to avoid reporting requirements. Forfeiture of laundered property authorized.

statute_title: Sexual Assault in the First Degree
elements: Defendant subjected another person to sexual intrusion
Through forcible compulsion
And caused submission by threat of death, serious bodily injury, or kidnapping
notes: First degree sexual assault is the most serious sexual offense. Second degree (§ 6-2-303) carries up to 20 years for sexual intrusion through forcible compulsion.

statute_title: Sexual Assault in the First Degree
elements: Defendant subjected another person to sexual intrusion
Through forcible compulsion
Causing submission by threat or use of physical force
notes: Wyoming uses 'sexual assault' rather than 'rape.' Sex offender registration required under § 7-19-302.

elements: Defendant exposed private parts in a public place
Under circumstances likely to cause affront or alarm
enhancements: In the presence of a minor
notes: Repeat offenses or exposure involving minors may trigger sex offender registration.

elements: Defendant offered or agreed to pay a fee
For the purpose of engaging in sexual conduct
notes: Promoting prostitution is a felony. Soliciting a minor triggers human trafficking charges.

elements: Defendant knowingly caused, induced, or permitted a child to engage in sexually explicit conduct
For the purpose of producing a visual depiction
notes: Possession of child pornography (§ 6-4-303(d)) is also a felony. Distribution carries enhanced penalties.

statute_title: Failure to Register as a Sex Offender
elements: Defendant was required to register as a sex offender
Defendant knowingly failed to register or update registration
notes: Registration requirements under § 7-19-302. Must register within 3 business days of release or relocation.

statute_title: Sexual Assault in the Third Degree (Statutory)
elements: Defendant, aged 18 or older, subjected another person to sexual intrusion or contact
Victim was under age of consent (16 years)
Defendant was at least 4 years older than the victim
enhancements: Victim under 13 (first degree — up to 50 years)
notes: Wyoming's age of consent is 16. Close-in-age exception (4-year gap). Sexual assault of a child under 13 is first-degree sexual assault.

elements: Defendant disturbed the peace by violent, profane, indecent, or boisterous conduct
Or unreasonable noise
In a public place or affecting the public
notes: General catch-all for public disturbances. Common plea-down from more serious charges.

elements: A peace officer was performing official duties
Defendant knowingly interfered with, obstructed, or resisted the officer
enhancements: Causing bodily injury to officer (aggravated assault charges)
notes: Wyoming uses 'interference with a peace officer' rather than 'resisting arrest.' Assault on a peace officer may be charged as aggravated assault.

statute_title: Obstruction of Justice / Compounding a Crime
elements: Defendant knowingly gave false information to an officer
Or concealed, destroyed, or altered evidence
With intent to hinder an investigation or prosecution
notes: Witness tampering and evidence destruction are felonies. Providing false information to an officer is a misdemeanor.

elements: Defendant willfully disobeyed a lawful court order
Or engaged in disorderly conduct in the presence of the court
notes: Direct contempt (in court's presence) may be punished summarily. Constructive contempt requires notice and hearing.

elements: Defendant was intoxicated in a public place
And was causing a disturbance or endangering self or others
notes: Public intoxication alone may not be criminal — typically requires accompanying disorderly conduct or danger to self/others.

offense_class: Misdemeanor (if underlying is misdemeanor); Felony (if underlying is felony)
elements: Defendant was released on bail or recognizance
Defendant willfully failed to appear as required by the court
notes: Bail jumping severity matches the underlying charge. Bail bond forfeited. Bench warrant issued.

elements: Defendant knowingly made a false report to law enforcement
Regarding the commission of a crime
notes: Filing a false police report is a misdemeanor. False bomb threats or emergency reports carry enhanced penalties.

elements: Defendant threatened to commit a violent felony
With intent to terrorize another person
Or cause evacuation of a building, place of assembly, or facility of public transportation
notes: Terroristic threats are a felony in Wyoming. Bomb threats and threats causing public panic carry enhanced penalties.

elements: Defendant made a materially false statement
Under oath in an official proceeding
Knowing the statement was false
notes: Subornation of perjury carries the same penalties. False swearing in non-official proceedings is a lesser offense.

elements: Defendant offered, gave, or promised something of value
To a public servant or official
With intent to influence the official's actions or decisions
notes: Accepting a bribe is also a felony. Includes bribery of jurors and witnesses.

elements: Defendant was lawfully in custody or confined
Defendant escaped from custody or confinement
enhancements: Use of force or violence during escape (enhanced to 10 years)
notes: Sentence runs consecutive to original sentence. Failure to return from furlough or work release is also escape.

elements: Defendant intentionally and maliciously tortured, injured, or killed an animal
Or neglected an animal causing unnecessary suffering
enhancements: Aggravated cruelty — torture or sadistic conduct (felony)
notes: Aggravated animal cruelty is a felony. Wyoming also has specific statutes for animal fighting.

offense_class: Varies — court may revoke probation and impose original sentence
elements: Defendant was placed on probation
Defendant violated a condition of probation
notes: Court has discretion to modify conditions, extend probation, or revoke and impose original sentence. New criminal charges typically result in revocation.

offense_class: Varies — return to prison for remaining term
elements: Defendant was released on parole
Defendant violated a condition of parole
notes: Board of Parole conducts revocation hearing. Technical violations may result in graduated sanctions before revocation.

elements: Defendant aided, abetted, counseled, or procured another person
To commit a crime
With intent that the crime be committed
notes: An accessory before the fact is punished as a principal. Accessory after the fact (§ 6-5-202) faces lesser penalties.

offense_class: One grade below the target offense
penalty_max: Maximum for one grade below target offense
elements: Defendant had intent to commit a specific crime
Defendant performed an overt act toward commission
Act went beyond mere preparation
notes: Attempt is punished at one grade below the completed offense. Voluntary abandonment is an affirmative defense.

offense_class: Same as target offense (felony); Misdemeanor (if target is misdemeanor)
elements: Defendant agreed with one or more persons to commit a crime
An overt act was performed in furtherance of the agreement
notes: Conspiracy requires an overt act. Conspiracy to commit a felony is a felony.
